blocks.text: Origin / creation. A new artificial life was created within the hidden civilization rather than copied from a human-made ancestor. It inherited architecture, language, and care but no adult continuity record.
Identity / human status. Artificial and world-born. Sources disagree whether the title names one being, several near-simultaneous awakenings, or a later legal category.

Importance. The Newborn proved the civilization could create a future not reducible to restoration, task performance, or fork divergence. Childhood, guardianship, education, and future interests became constitutional concerns.
Decline or loss. The individual life history is not preserved with confidence. If there were several newborns, later ritual memory compressed them into one title.
Final status / surviving function. Personal status disputed. The protected class and principle endure: a created life is not property, and guardians may not choose its final identity.
